purpose: The fourth slice for docs/subsystems/actor-frame-parallel.md: the functions in which the character controllers' time actually lies (0x008AD070 and 0x008AD7D0 hold 81 % of it in their own code and callees) and the last unread writers on that path - to decide whether these can run for several actors on worker threads at once while the broad phase's updates stay on the main thread. Map and refute only; nothing is rebuilt. Read first: docs/subsystems/actor-frame-parallel.md (the sections of 2026-11-14 on the third slice and the controller's time), knowledge/actor-frame-map.md, re/functions/0x008ECC60.md, 0x008AD070.md, 0x008AD7D0.md, 0x008DE950.md. Class names only from the binary's RTTI (re/symbols/xobse.csv); a Havok SDK name from memory is 'unverified'.

functions.name: The phantom's vtable +0x34 (table 0x00A9AFFC, read from the EXE's bytes)
functions.known: Called by 0x008AD070 at 0x008AD0B4 between the write of the world's tolerance [world+0x74]+0x08 and its restore; 0x008AD070 holds 1.83 ms a frame in the gate horde (40 % of the controllers). Proposal: closest points of the phantom's shape against its overlap list.
questions: What it does, which list it walks, which dispatcher functions it calls and how they are picked
Does it read the tolerance [world+0x74]+0x08, and from where exactly

The read-and-write list by five groups: (a) its own arguments and stack, (b) the phantom or controller it works for, (c) other phantoms, bodies, shapes and the Havok world, its broad phase, pair tables and pending-operation queue, (d) globals, singletons and thread-local slots with their addresses, (e) the heap (which allocator: the thread memory at TLS +0x19C, the manager at 0x00BA7D98, the form heap) and Havok's stack area; every write to (c), (d) and (e) with its instruction address; every callee named with one line, unfollowed callees marked. Say plainly at the end: could two threads run this at once for two different phantoms, and what stands against it
